title: RT-MDM: Real-Time Scheduling Framework for Multi-DNN on MCU Using External Memory
problem: Multiple DNN tasks must be scheduled on resource-constrained microcontroller units while meeting real-time deadlines and managing limited external memory. Existing systems lack execution-order dependency awareness and efficient memory sharing policies for parallel DNN execution.
motivation: As DNN applications extend to time-critical embedded systems, providing timing guarantees is essential for safety-critical deployments.
method: RT-MDM breaks deep neural networks (AI models) into segments and determines which segments must run in a specific order to produce correct results. It groups these segments and manages memory by assigning separate memory space to each group, while allowing groups to reuse each other's memory once they finish. A specialized scheduler optimizes how to split the networks into segments and arrange them into groups, aiming to run as many concurrent tasks as possible while ensuring all meet their deadlines.
key_novelty: The first real-time scheduler that runs multiple deep neural networks (AI models) on microcontroller units (MCUs) by managing the sequence in which each model segment must run and efficiently sharing memory across segments to meet timing deadlines.
contributions: First real-time scheduling framework for multiple DNN tasks on MCUs using external memory
Segment-group-based memory management achieving both isolated and shared memory policies
Specialized intra-task scheduler adapted to the proposed memory management approach
System implementation demonstrating increased DNN task accommodation with timing guarantees

metrics.other: number of accommodated tasks with timing guarantees

limitations: Specific baseline systems and detailed comparative evaluation not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: real-time multi-DNN scheduling on embedded MCUs
